data.title: The Euler brick
data.statement:
The Euler brick is a special kind of brick where not only are the [[length]], [[width]] and [[height]] of the brick all integers, but so are the diagonals on all <<faces>>.

For a <<face>> with side lengths a and b, you can think of the diagonal length c as the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the other two sides having length a and b, and use Pythagoras's Theorem "<<a^2 + b^2 = c^2>>"

Given the [[length]], [[width]] and [[height]] of a brick, determine if it is an Euler brick. If the given values do not form a brick at all print {{Not a brick}}.

Example: A brick of lengths 44, 117 and 240 has <<face>> diagonals of 125, 244 and 267, making it an Euler brick.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

The Euler brick is a special kind of brick where not only are the length, width and height of the brick all integers, but so are the diagonals on all faces.

For a face with side lengths a and b, you can think of the diagonal length c as the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the other two sides having length a and b, and use Pythagoras's Theorem "a^2 + b^2 = c^2"

Given the length, width and height of a brick, determine if it is an Euler brick. If the given values do not form a brick at all print Not a brick.

Example: A brick of lengths 44, 117 and 240 has face diagonals of 125, 244 and 267, making it an Euler brick.
Input
Line 1: An integer for the length of a brick.
Line 2: An integer for the width of a brick.
Line 3: An integer for the height of a brick.
Output
Line 1: Euler brick if the brick in question is an Euler brick, Regular brick if not, Not a brick if the given inputs do not make a brick.
Constraints
0 <= length,width,height <= 100000
Example
Input
44
117
240
Output
Euler brick
